sections.F: Lost photons, faster routes and leaks
sections.G: Beyond basic BB84: more protocols, real sites, faulty verifiers

demos.title: A1 · Prover exactly in the middle
demos.watch: Both verifiers are 3 m away, so they send at the same moment and both signals meet at P.

demos.title: A2 · Prover closer to one verifier
demos.watch: V1 is only 1 m away, so it sends later than V0. Open the Timing tab: both still reach P together.

demos.title: A3 · Claim outside the verifiers
demos.watch: The claim is 10 m out, past V1. A cheater standing next to V1 gets both signals first and answers early. Claims must lie between the verifiers.

demos.title: A3 · Claim off to the side
demos.watch: The claim is 2 m to the side of the road. A cheater on the road is closer to both verifiers, so it passes. Two verifiers only check the position along their line.

demos.title: A4 · Prover right at a verifier
demos.watch: The claim is V0's own spot. It works, but it only proves 'someone is next to V0'.

demos.title: A5 · 3D: four verifiers around the prover
demos.watch: Four verifiers, not on one plane, surround the claim. Rotate the 3D view in the Geometry tab.

demos.title: A7 · Prover 4 cm off, inside the precision
demos.expect: Accepted every round, with a thin margin.
demos.watch: An allowance of 0.5 ns minus 0.2 ns of processing leaves about ±4.5 cm. 4 cm still fits.

demos.title: A7 · Prover 6 cm off, beyond the precision
demos.expect: Rejected every round: the answer to V1 is late.
demos.watch: 6 cm is just past the precision limit, so the honest prover's answer misses V1's deadline.

demos.title: B1 · Prover moved 3 cm (10% of light speed for 1 ns)
demos.watch: Positions are fixed during a run, so this shows where a very fast prover would be when it answers. At everyday speeds the movement within a round is nanometres.

demos.title: B1 · Walking prover, verifiers don't follow it
demos.expect: The first 33 of 100 rounds pass, then every round fails.
demos.watch: The prover walks at 1.4 m/s and rounds are 1 ms apart, but the verifiers keep aiming at the starting spot. After about 33 rounds it is more than 4.5 cm away, beyond the precision. Press Play 100 rounds.

demos.title: B1 · Walking prover, verifiers follow its path
demos.watch: Same walk, but each round aims at where the prover should be by then. Press Play 100 rounds: all pass.

demos.title: B2 · Prover takes 0.8 ns to respond
demos.watch: The allowance is 0.5 ns, but the prover needs 0.8 ns. Add a 'Change the time allowance' twist of 1 ns and it passes, with a blurrier location.

demos.title: B3 · V1's clock is 1 ns ahead
demos.expect: V0 accepts, V1 rejects, so the claim is rejected.
demos.watch: V1 sends 1 ns early and also stops waiting 1 ns early. Change the offset to 0.2 ns and it passes.

demos.title: B4 · V1 uses fibre and adjusts for it
demos.watch: V1's link runs at 2/3 of light speed. V1 sends about 5 ns earlier and waits 5 ns longer, so the honest prover passes.

demos.title: B4 · Fibre adjustment exploited by a cheater
demos.expect: The cheater passes every round from 70 cm away.
demos.watch: V1 allows 5 ns for fibre, but the cheater relays through open air at full speed. The spare time lets it pass from 70 cm away instead of a few cm.

demos.title: B5 · Noisy channel (15% errors)
demos.expect: About 85% of rounds accepted, the same as the best cheaters without entanglement.
demos.watch: Press Play 100 rounds. At 15% errors an honest prover looks just like a cheater.

demos.title: B5 · 2% errors, judged over 360 rounds
demos.expect: About 98% per round; passes the 360-round test practically always.
demos.watch: With 2% errors the verifiers cannot demand every round right. Accepting 337 of 360 lets an honest prover through and stops the best cheaters without entanglement (see the next case). 'qpv rounds --honest 0.98 --cheat 0.854' works this out.

demos.title: B5 · The same 360-round test against the best cheaters
demos.expect: About 84% per round; fails the 360-round test practically always (well under one in a million).
demos.watch: The cheaters win most rounds, but not 93.6% of them. Press Play 100 rounds and read the many-round line.

demos.title: B6 · 60% of photons lost
demos.expect: About 40% of rounds accepted; the rest get no answer.
demos.watch: Press Play 100 rounds. When the photon is lost the prover has nothing to answer, and the verifiers time out.

demos.title: B7 · The laser sends two photons
demos.watch: With two copies, each cheater keeps one, waits for the basis and reads it correctly.

demos.title: B7 · Weak laser (0.5 photons per pulse), honest prover
demos.expect: About 39% of rounds; the rest are empty pulses with no answer.
demos.watch: Each pulse holds a random number of photons, on average 0.5. With no photon there is nothing to read (1 − e^−0.5 ≈ 39% of pulses have one or more).

demos.title: B7 · Weak laser, cheaters wait for two-photon pulses
demos.expect: About 9% of rounds pass, never with a wrong answer.
demos.watch: The cheaters block every pulse with fewer than two photons and use two-photon pulses to read the bit for sure. The verifiers just see more loss, so a loss threshold alone cannot catch them.

demos.title: B7 · Detector false clicks (10%)
demos.watch: A false click beside the real one gives a double click, recorded as a random bit, so 10% false clicks cost about 5% of rounds.

demos.title: B8 · Why many rounds matter
demos.expect: About 85% per round; almost never 100 in a row.
demos.watch: Press Play 100 rounds. Passing all 100 would happen about once in 7.5 million tries.

demos.title: B8 · 88 rounds against the best cheaters
demos.expect: About 85% per round; passes all 88 rounds about once in a million.
demos.watch: Each round on its own looks good for the cheaters. Demanding all 88 rounds right leaves them a one-in-a-million chance.

demos.title: C1 · Lone cheater on V1's side
demos.watch: It must answer V0 before V0's photon could reach it, so that answer is a coin flip.

demos.title: C1 · Lone cheater on V0's side
demos.watch: It gets the photon early but not the basis, so it reads it in the Breidbart basis.

demos.title: C2 · Two cheaters guessing the basis
demos.watch: Right basis half the time, a coin flip otherwise.

demos.title: C2 · Two cheaters, best possible strategy
demos.watch: No strategy without entanglement can do better than cos²(π/8) ≈ 85%.

demos.title: C3 · Eavesdropper reads and resends the photon
demos.expect: The honest prover passes about 75% of rounds.
demos.watch: When the eavesdropper guesses the wrong basis, the photon it sends on is random. This is sabotage, not impersonation.

demos.title: C4 · Cheaters who just guess
demos.watch: Each cheater answers a random bit; both have to be right.

demos.title: D1 · Teleportation with one entangled pair
demos.watch: The photon is teleported before anyone knows the basis; the fix-up afterwards is ordinary bits.

demos.title: D3 · Teleportation chain in 2D (XOR basis)
demos.watch: Splitting the basis into XOR pieces doesn't help: a chain of teleports still wins.

demos.title: D4 · Poor entanglement (50% noise)
demos.expect: About 75% of rounds, worse than cheating without entanglement.
demos.watch: The shared pair is half noise (quality p = 0.5). Teleporting through it adds errors: (1 + p)/2 = 75% right.

demos.title: D4 · Good entanglement (10% noise)
demos.watch: Quality p = 0.9. Above p ≈ 0.71 (below about 29% noise), imperfect entanglement already beats the 85% limit.

demos.title: E1 · Cheater standing at the claimed spot
demos.watch: Position checking proves where, not who. Adding a secret key would be needed to check identity.

demos.title: E1 · Impostor at the claimed spot, answers need a key
demos.watch: The real prover shares a fresh 8-bit key with the verifiers each round and attaches it to its answer. The impostor is in the right place but has to guess the key.

demos.title: E1 · Genuine prover with the key
demos.watch: The prover holding the key passes as before. The key proves who answered; the timing still proves where.

demos.title: E3 · Someone in the middle flips the basis
demos.expect: The honest prover passes about 50% of rounds.
demos.watch: The prover reads with the wrong setting and gets random answers. The verifiers notice errors.

demos.title: E3 · Someone in the middle holds messages for 2 ns
demos.watch: Delaying only blocks the check. It can never make a cheater pass.

demos.title: E4 · Cheater right next to V0
demos.watch: Being near a verifier gives no extra advantage. It is the lone cheater of C1.

demos.title: E5 · Honest prover and cheater at the same spot
demos.expect: Accepted: the cheater got the photon and answered.
demos.watch: Both get the basis, but only one can have the photon. The honest prover is left waiting.

demos.title: F1 · Cheaters say 'no photon' when they guess wrong
demos.expect: About 50% accepted, 50% 'lost', no wrong answers; passes a 200-round test that allows 60% loss.
demos.watch: Press Play 100 rounds and check the outcomes: lost rounds, but never a wrong bit. With real loss above 50%, verifiers can't tell this from an honest prover.

demos.title: F2 · Four bases: honest prover with 50% loss
demos.expect: About 50% answered, all correct; passes the 200-round test.
demos.watch: V0 now picks one of four bases. Half the photons are lost and the prover says so. The test asks for at least 40% of rounds answered and 95% of those right.

demos.title: F2 · Four bases: selective 'no photon' cheaters caught
demos.expect: About 25% answered; fails the 200-round test practically always.
demos.watch: Guessing one basis in four is right only a quarter of the time, so the cheaters must claim 75% loss, more than the test allows. With two bases (F1) they got away with 50%.

demos.title: F3 · Cheater with a straight route past a 12 m fibre detour
demos.expect: The cheater passes every round from next to V0.
demos.watch: V1 allows 50 ns for its fibre detour. The cheater takes the straight path and has time to spare.

demos.title: F4 · The basis leaks to a cheater
demos.watch: Knowing the basis early, it reads the photon the moment it arrives. Verifier secrets must stay secret.

demos.title: G1 · Six-state protocol (3 bases) against cheaters without entanglement
demos.expect: About 67% of rounds (85% with two bases).
demos.watch: The verifiers pick one of three bases, Z, X or Y. Guessing the basis is right only a third of the time, so the cheaters' best simple strategy drops from 85% to 2/3.

demos.title: G1 · Qudit with 8 levels (9 bases) against the same cheaters
demos.watch: The photon now carries one of 8 values (on 3 qubits) in one of 9 bases. A wrong basis guess gives a random value out of 8, so guessing cheaters get 2/9.

demos.title: G1 · Qudit with 4 levels, honest prover in 2D
demos.watch: Three verifiers around the claim; the basis is the sum of two shares mod 5. The honest prover waits for everything and measures in the right basis.

demos.title: G1 · Qudit with 4 levels: two entangled pairs still break it
demos.watch: Bigger quantum systems make guessing harder but do not stop teleportation: two EPR pairs carry the 4-level qudit, and the Bell results tell the cheaters how the outcome was shuffled.

demos.title: G2 · BB84^f, random f with 3-bit strings: cheaters with 1 EPR pair
demos.expect: About 87% of rounds: barely better than without entanglement.
demos.watch: V0 sends the photon and a 3-bit string x, V1 a 3-bit string y; the basis is f(x, y). The generic attack needs a pair for every possible x (8). With 1 pair it only helps when x = 0. Use Chart... with 'EPR pairs' to see the climb to 100%.

demos.title: G2 · The same protocol: cheaters with all 8 EPR pairs
demos.watch: With one pair for every possible x, E0 teleports the photon into pair x and E1 measures every pair j in basis f(j, y). The honest prover still handles one photon and 6 bits; the attack needs 2^n pairs.

demos.title: G2 · A bad choice of f: xor of parities falls to one EPR pair
demos.watch: If f(x, y) = parity(x) xor parity(y), E0 can apply its half of the basis before teleporting, so one pair is enough. The function f must be hard, not just long.

demos.title: G3 · Classical position verification: colluders always win
demos.watch: Without a qubit there is nothing that cannot be copied: each colluder forwards its verifier's bit and everyone answers the xor in time. This is why position verification needs quantum physics.

demos.title: G4 · University campus with free-space links (400 m)
demos.expect: About 80% of rounds (the detector misses 20% of photons); location known to about ±9 cm.
demos.watch: Three verifiers on rooftops 400 m from the claim send light straight through the air. Open the Geometry map: positions come from real coordinates.

demos.title: G4 · City centre over street fibre (5 km)
demos.expect: About 57% of rounds (43% of photons lost); location known only to about ±3 km.
demos.watch: The verifiers reach the claim through fibre that winds 1.5 times the straight distance at 2/3 of light speed. They allow for it by sending early, which hands anyone with a straight path about 20 µs to spare.

demos.title: G4 · City centre: an impostor 2 km from the claim
demos.expect: The impostor passes every round, more often than the honest prover.
demos.watch: Standing 2 km away with straight line-of-sight links, the impostor still answers in time, and loses no photons in fibre. Over fibre, the check proves almost nothing.

demos.title: G5 · One verifier offline, all three must accept
demos.watch: V2 sends its share but never reports. With the rule 'all must accept', one broken verifier blocks every honest prover.

demos.title: G5 · The same broken verifier, 2 of 3 must accept
demos.watch: Requiring only two of the three verifiers keeps the system working while V2 is down.

demos.title: G5 · A corrupt verifier that accepts anything, all must accept
demos.expect: Guessing cheaters pass about 25% of rounds instead of 12.5%.
demos.watch: V2 approves every answer, so the guessers only have to fool V0 and V1.

demos.title: G5 · The same corrupt verifier under a 2-of-3 rule
demos.expect: Guessing cheaters pass about 75% of rounds.
demos.watch: With 2 of 3 required and V2 approving everything, one lucky guess at V0 or V1 is enough. Tolerating broken verifiers makes a corrupt one far more dangerous.
